hero.headline: Oil Prices Rise as U.S. Reinstates Iran Blockade in Strait of Hormuz
hero.body:
Oil prices jumped sharply after the United States reinstated its blockade on Iranian shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, following the collapse of a ceasefire agreement between the two nations. The escalating tensions have sent ripples through global energy markets and beyond.

Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, rose nearly 6 percent to more than $80 a barrel on Wednesday, marking the highest price since the U.S. and Iran had agreed to a ceasefire last month. The price increase came after Iran launched attacks on at least three tankers transiting the strait within 48 hours, including a vessel carrying liquified natural gas. In response, President Trump declared the ceasefire deal over and reinstated the blockade.

The Strait of Hormuz is a critical maritime chokepoint where roughly one-fifth of global oil supplies pass through each day. The renewed tensions have essentially halted tanker traffic through the passage. According to ship-tracking data, at least four oil and gas tankers have turned back from attempting to transit the strait, disrupting efforts to restore normal flows after months of previous disruption.

The impact extends beyond oil markets. UK short-dated bonds suffered their worst day since March as markets priced in the likelihood of a Bank of England rate increase to combat renewed inflation pressures. The FTSE 100 index fell nearly 1.7 percent, its biggest single-day drop since May, as concerns grew about the economic fallout from escalating tensions. However, oil and gas companies bucked the trend, with BP rising 3.5 percent and Shell climbing 2.2 percent.

Energy prices spiked across the board. In Europe, natural gas market prices jumped 5 percent, with the benchmark Dutch contract rising more than 2.40 euros to 49 euros per megawatt hour. The UK gas equivalent rose by 6 pence to 116.75 pence per therm. These increases threaten to raise household costs, which have already faced the steepest summer energy bill increases in four years.

According to analysts at Rystad Energy, tanker traffic has essentially stopped, reflecting heightened risk perception rather than any single statement from either government. The critical test will come after Iran's supreme leader's burial ceremony later in the week, when both nations will signal whether they still have appetite for a diplomatic resolution.

Some analysts remain cautiously optimistic. Market experts note that global oil markets have demonstrated resilience to disruption, with alternative supply routes and emergency measures helping offset previous blockade impacts. However, the situation remains fluid, with shipping companies and governments assessing potential duration and alternative solutions to restore critical energy supplies through the strait.

cards.headline: Ukrainian Strikes Target Russian Ships in Campaign to Isolate Crimea
cards.teaser: Ukraine intensified drone attacks on Russian naval vessels and oil infrastructure in an effort to sever supply lines to occupied Crimea.
cards.body:
Ukrainian forces launched extensive drone strikes against Russian shipping in the Sea of Azov and attacked oil facilities as part of an ongoing campaign to cut off Russian supply routes to Crimea. The operations targeted both military vessels and commercial tankers carrying fuel, with multiple oil tankers set ablaze in recent attacks.

The strikes represent a systematic effort by Ukraine to disrupt Russian logistics supporting forces in the Crimean Peninsula. The campaign has focused on chokepoints in the Sea of Azov, a critical waterway for Russian military and commercial shipping. Recent days have seen both countries launch attacks on each other's infrastructure for transporting goods.

cards.headline: Trump administration renews military pressure on Iran over Strait of Hormuz
cards.teaser: President Trump is restarting confrontation with Iran in an effort to break its control over the strategic shipping channel.
cards.body:
President Trump is escalating military pressure against Iran in a bid to challenge its control over the Strait of Hormuz, a vital global oil shipping route. This represents a return to confrontational tactics from his earlier administration.

In response, Iran threatened to block all oil export routes in the region, citing the U.S. maritime blockade of Iranian ports. The renewed standoff echoes a pattern of military and economic pressure that has now persisted for more than four months, with experts questioning whether this approach will succeed where previous efforts did not.

cards.headline: Microsoft patches record 622 security flaws including two actively exploited vulnerabilities
cards.teaser: Microsoft released security updates addressing 622 vulnerabilities in its software products, the largest number of fixes the company has issued in a single mont.
cards.body:
Microsoft released security updates addressing 622 vulnerabilities in its software products, the largest number of fixes the company has issued in a single monthly update cycle. The patches include fixes for two zero-day vulnerabilities that attackers have already exploited in the wild.

The update cycle tripled the previous record set in June, when Microsoft patched approximately 207 vulnerabilities. The company releases security updates on the second Tuesday of each month, known as Patch Tuesday, to address newly discovered flaws in Windows, Office, and other Microsoft products.

The two zero-day vulnerabilities under active attack represent the most urgent threats in this month's batch. Zero-day flaws are security weaknesses that attackers exploit before the software vendor becomes aware of them or can issue a fix. Microsoft did not disclose specific details about how attackers used these vulnerabilities or which systems were targeted.

The unprecedented volume of patches reflects growing security challenges for software companies as their products become more complex and interconnected. Each vulnerability represents a potential entry point for attackers to gain unauthorized access to systems, steal data, or disrupt operations. Security researchers and attackers continuously probe popular software for weaknesses, leading to an ongoing cycle of discovery and repair.

Microsoft recommends that organizations and individual users apply the security updates as quickly as possible, particularly for the actively exploited vulnerabilities. The company provides automated update mechanisms through Windows Update for consumer systems and enterprise management tools for organizations. System administrators typically test patches in controlled environments before deploying them widely to ensure they do not interfere with critical business operations.

cards.headline: Google to allow rival app stores on Android devices starting next week
cards.teaser: Google and Epic Games withdrew their legal efforts to modify a court injunction that will require Google Play to open to third-party app stores.
cards.body:
Google and Epic Games have jointly withdrawn their attempt to modify a court injunction, clearing the way for third-party app stores to operate on Android starting next week. The decision ends the legal battle between the two companies and forces Google to allow competing app stores within its ecosystem.

The change marks a significant shift in how Android distributes applications. For years, the Google Play Store served as the dominant marketplace for Android apps. Under the new arrangement, rival app stores will be able to operate alongside Google's platform, offering users alternative ways to discover and download applications.

The withdrawal of the joint settlement attempt is notable because both companies had sought to retroactively change the terms of the lawsuit that originally mandated this shift. By abandoning that effort, they've allowed the original court order to take effect as written. Google confirmed to the court that it is prepared to implement the requirement beginning next week.

This development represents one of the most substantial restructurings of Android's app distribution model in the platform's history. Third-party app stores will operate what developers and industry observers describe as a "store-within-a-store" arrangement, meaning users will be able to access multiple app marketplaces directly through their devices.

The case between Google and Epic Games has been a landmark antitrust dispute, with Epic challenging Google's control over app distribution on Android. The legal battle led to the original injunction requiring Google to open its platform to competitors. By not pursuing the modification they initially sought, both companies have effectively accepted that outcome.

The timing of the implementation next week suggests Google has completed its technical preparations to integrate third-party app stores into the Android experience. The company will need to ensure that these rival stores can function properly within its ecosystem while maintaining security and performance standards.

This move could have far-reaching implications for app developers, who will gain additional channels through which to reach Android users. It may also provide consumers with more choices in how they access applications and potentially more competitive pricing or exclusive offerings through different marketplaces.

The decision reflects broader regulatory pressure on major tech platforms worldwide to open their ecosystems to competition. Android's shift toward allowing rival app stores joins similar changes happening across the technology industry, where regulators have increasingly scrutinized the gatekeeping power of large platforms.

As these third-party app stores begin operating next week, the Android ecosystem will look substantially different from its current configuration. Users will face new options for downloading apps, while developers will have additional opportunities to distribute their work outside Google's direct control.

cards.headline: Major U.S. Automakers Pull Back From Electric Vehicles as Global Sales Boom
cards.teaser: The largest American car manufacturers have reduced their electric vehicle commitments even as worldwide EV sales continue to grow rapidly.
cards.body:
The largest U.S. automakers have reduced their investment in electric vehicle production at a time when global EV sales continue to accelerate. Manufacturers in Europe and Asia are expanding their electric vehicle portfolios and gaining market share during this shift.

The pullback by American automakers raises questions about their competitiveness as the industry transitions toward electrification and consumer preferences evolve. Industry analysts warn that this strategic retreat could disadvantage U.S. manufacturers in the long term.

cards.headline: Forecast shows Democrats winning House, Senate split 50-50 in November
cards.teaser: A new projection from Decision Desk HQ puts Democrats on track to take the House while the Senate heads toward an even partisan divide.
cards.body:
Decision Desk HQ projects Democrats will win control of the House while the Senate remains evenly divided between the two parties heading into November's midterm elections. The forecast underscores how competitive the battle for Congress will be over 100 days before voters go to the polls.

A 50-50 Senate would leave the chamber deadlocked, with Vice President Kamala Harris holding the tie-breaking vote to determine which party controls the chamber. Democratic control of the House would allow the party to shape the legislative agenda and lead congressional committees.

hero.headline: China's Economic Growth Falls Short of Target
hero.teaser: China missed its economic growth target as weak domestic demand and rising oil prices from the Iran conflict offset strong export performance.
hero.body:
China's economic growth has slowed sharply, missing government targets. Weak domestic demand and rising oil prices stemming from the Iran conflict have weighed on the economy, despite the country maintaining strong export performance.

The slowdown underscores the pressure facing Chinese policymakers as they navigate competing economic challenges at home and abroad.

cards.headline: Russian Bombing Kills Three in Odesa
cards.teaser: Three people died in continued Russian strikes on the Ukrainian port city of Odesa as both countries targeted shipping infrastructure.
cards.body:
Russian bombing of Odesa killed three people as part of ongoing attacks on the Ukrainian port city. In recent days, Russia and Ukraine have launched strikes against each other's shipping infrastructure.

Odesa remains a critical target in the conflict, serving as a major port for Ukrainian maritime trade on the Black Sea. Both sides have intensified their campaign to damage the other's ability to move goods and supplies by sea.

cards.headline: Australia Moves to Regulate Data Centers Amid AI Expansion
cards.teaser: Australia will impose energy and water limits on data centers while seeking protections for creators whose work trains AI models.
cards.body:
The Australian government is introducing energy and water usage restrictions for data centers as AI development accelerates across the country. The regulations will also address protections for creators whose work is used to train AI models.

The initiative addresses environmental concerns tied to AI's expansion, as data centers require substantial electricity for computing and water for cooling systems. These new guardrails aim to establish sustainable parameters for the growing industry.

cards.headline: Six Die in Elevator During Brussels Office Building Fire
cards.teaser: Six bodies were discovered in an elevator after a fire broke out at the Oxy building in central Brussels.
cards.body:
A fire at the Oxy building in central Brussels on Tuesday morning resulted in six deaths. Emergency responders discovered the bodies in an elevator after extinguishing the blaze at the city center office building.

Investigators are working to determine how the victims became trapped in the elevator during the fire. High-rise building fires create serious risks when evacuation routes are blocked or building systems malfunction.

cards.headline: Bangkok Bar Fire Death Toll Rises to 30 Amid Safety Questions
cards.teaser: Investigators are examining whether flammable foam and blocked exits contributed to a Bangkok bar fire that killed 30 people.
cards.body:
The death toll from a Bangkok music bar fire has reached 30, with more than 70 people injured and 24 remaining in critical condition. An initial assessment found that an electrical short circuit in an air conditioner located in the ceiling sparked the blaze, the city's deadliest fire in 17 years.

Police have identified negligence as their primary theory of investigation. The bar owner has offered apologies and pledged cooperation with authorities examining whether emergency exits were blocked or difficult to access. Officials are also scrutinizing construction materials and evacuation procedures at the venue.

cards.headline: Sierra Leone Drops Treason Charge Against Former President
cards.teaser: Ernest Bai Koroma will no longer face treason charges connected to a 2023 attempted coup in which gunmen raided an armory and freed inmates.
cards.body:
Sierra Leone has dropped treason charges against former President Ernest Bai Koroma. Koroma was arrested in 2023 following an armed incident in which gunmen broke into a military armory and several prisons, freeing inmates in the process.

The treason charge was the most serious criminal accusation Koroma faced in connection with the attempted coup. The government's decision to drop the charges marks a significant development in how it is handling legal proceedings related to the 2023 incident.

hero.headline: DHS requires body cameras on all ICE arrest teams after fatal shootings
hero.body:
The Department of Homeland Security announced that every Immigration and Customs Enforcement arrest team will now include at least one agent equipped with a body camera. Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem said on Monday that federal agents in Minneapolis will immediately begin wearing the cameras, with the program expanding nationwide "as funding is available."

The policy shift comes after two fatal shootings by ICE agents drew intense scrutiny. The shootings of Alex Pretti and Renee Good in recent operations sparked debate over transparency and accountability in immigration enforcement. The incidents occurred during ICE patrols that have faced fierce criticism for their tactics in Minneapolis and elsewhere.

The announcement represents a significant concession to Democratic lawmakers who have made body cameras a key condition for approving continued funding of the Department of Homeland Security. Republican Senator Ron Johnson of Wisconsin, who chairs the Senate's homeland security committee, indicated support for the measure. "I don't have a problem with that personally," Johnson told CNN, acknowledging that cameras could help clarify disputed situations.

President Trump also signaled backing for body cameras. "They generally tend to be good for law enforcement because people can't lie about what's happening," he said during a White House event.

Democratic leaders have attached multiple reform conditions to their agreement on homeland security funding. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer has called for ending roving patrols and requiring judicial warrants before agents enter homes to conduct arrests. He has also demanded that agents be prohibited from wearing masks and carry proper identification. Additionally, Democrats have pushed for a universal code of conduct governing the use of force by federal law enforcement officers.

Schumer has characterized these proposals as "commonsense changes," warning that Republican refusal to support them amounts to "choosing chaos over order."

Agents have faced criticism for arresting and pepper-spraying demonstrators and people filming or following them. Civil rights lawyers argue these activities are protected under the First Amendment.

Johnson rejected the judicial warrant requirement, calling it a "sneaky way" to undermine immigration enforcement. He argued that immigration cases have traditionally been handled through administrative judges rather than the criminal court system, and that imposing additional barriers would exacerbate existing case backlogs.

House Democratic leaders have continued pushing for ICE reforms. Hakeem Jeffries, the House Democrats' leader, told ABC News that "ICE agents should conduct themselves like every other law enforcement agency in the country." He criticized agents for what he called acting like "masked thugs" engaged in brutality against law-abiding citizens.

The Senate passed a spending package last Friday to fund government departments through September and approved a two-week continuation of homeland security operations. The House is expected to consider the legislation this week, with Democrats anticipated to continue demanding ICE reforms.

cards.headline: Trump administration scales back immigration crackdown after ICE shootings
cards.teaser: The administration ordered ICE to halt most vehicle stops following two fatal shootings in Maine and Texas.
cards.body:
The Trump administration implemented new enforcement guidelines following two fatal shootings by ICE agents within a week. The directive requires ICE to halt most vehicle stops and mandates that every ICE arrest team include an agent equipped with a body camera.

The shootings drew significant attention, including a fatal incident in Maine involving a Colombian immigrant. The incidents have become a focal point in Maine's Senate race, with candidates addressing voter concerns about immigration enforcement operations and the use of force during arrests.

cards.headline: Todd Blanche faces Senate confirmation hearing for attorney general
cards.teaser: Blanche, currently the No. 2 official at the Justice Department, seeks confirmation as attorney general.
cards.body:
Todd Blanche appeared before the Senate Judiciary Committee for his confirmation hearing as President Trump's nominee for attorney general. Blanche previously won Senate confirmation to serve as deputy attorney general, the Justice Department's No. 2 position, early in Trump's second term.

Senators pressed Blanche on his record leading the department's day-to-day operations. During his tenure as deputy attorney general, career prosecutors were purged from the department, and its priorities shifted toward investigating political rivals and claims about the 2020 election. If confirmed, Blanche would become the nation's top law enforcement officer.

cards.headline: Trump intelligence nominee faces Senate confirmation hearing
cards.teaser: Jay Clayton testifies before lawmakers after a weekslong delay in the confirmation process.
cards.body:
Jay Clayton, President Trump's nominee to lead intelligence agencies, faces senators eager to see him replace the current director. The hearing comes after a weekslong delay in the confirmation process for the position overseeing the nation's intelligence community.

Clayton is expected to face tough questioning from senators about his qualifications and approach to intelligence oversight. The nomination has drawn attention as lawmakers weigh whether to confirm Trump's choice to head the intelligence agencies.

cards.headline: CDC director nominee appears before Senate health committee
cards.teaser: Dr. Erica Schwartz faces senators as she seeks confirmation to lead the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
cards.body:
Dr. Erica Schwartz appeared before the Senate health committee on July 15 for her confirmation hearing as Trump's nominee to lead the CDC. If confirmed, she would take the helm of an agency contending with workforce and leadership shortages.

The CDC is also operating under new layers of political review within the current administration. Schwartz would oversee the agency as it navigates staffing challenges and organizational changes.

cards.headline: Epstein survivor speaks out during Todd Blanche confirmation
cards.teaser: Dani Bensky and other women abused by Jeffrey Epstein have formed what they call a survivor sisterhood.
cards.body:
Dani Bensky and other women abused by Jeffrey Epstein have formed what they call a "survivor sisterhood." The group has become a visible presence during Todd Blanche's confirmation hearing as he seeks to become attorney general.

Blanche previously won Senate confirmation to serve as the No. 2 official at the Justice Department early in President Trump's second term. The survivors balance their advocacy work with personal lives that include motherhood, speaking publicly about their experiences as they navigate the confirmation process.

cards.headline: Some US startups switch to Chinese AI models to cut costs
cards.teaser: Companies are turning to cheaper Chinese artificial intelligence models as AI expenses grow rapidly.
cards.body:
Artificial intelligence has become a significant and rapidly growing business expense for companies. Facing high costs associated with American AI models, some US startups are turning to cheaper Chinese alternatives to manage their budgets more effectively.

The price gap between American and Chinese AI solutions is driving this shift as companies evaluate their technology spending. Businesses are weighing the financial savings from less expensive Chinese models as part of their broader AI strategy decisions.

cards.headline: China Economic Growth Falls Below Target Amid Weak Demand and Higher Oil Costs
cards.teaser: The country's quarterly growth missed expectations as weak domestic consumption and rising energy prices offset strong export performance.
cards.body:
China's economic growth fell sharply in the latest quarter, failing to meet the government's target. Weak domestic demand significantly hampered overall performance, even as the country maintained strong export figures.

Rising oil prices stemming from escalating U.S.-Iran tensions have added to economic pressures. The increased energy costs have raised production and transportation expenses for Chinese manufacturers, compounding challenges from reduced consumer confidence and spending at home.

cards.headline: ASML Raises Outlook and Expands Capacity on Strong AI Chip Demand
cards.teaser: The Dutch semiconductor equipment manufacturer increased its financial guidance as artificial intelligence applications drive demand for advanced chipmaking machinery.
cards.body:
ASML raised its outlook for 2026 and announced plans to expand production capacity in response to sustained demand for chip manufacturing equipment driven by artificial intelligence applications. The company reported 9.3 billion in total net sales and 2.9 billion in net income for the second quarter of 2026.

The guidance increase marks another upward revision as the company struggles to keep pace with orders from chipmakers racing to build capacity for AI processors. ASML manufactures extreme ultraviolet lithography machines essential for producing the most advanced semiconductors, giving it a unique position in the global chip supply chain.

cards.headline: Social Security Quietly Rebuilds After Losing Nearly 8,000 Workers to Budget Cuts
cards.teaser: The agency has begun hiring again and focusing on technology improvements to manage workloads following staff departures tied to DOGE initiative reductions.
cards.body:
The Social Security Administration is quietly rehiring workers after losing roughly 7,800 employees due to budget cuts imposed a year ago. The agency is now prioritizing technology improvements to help its smaller workforce handle existing demands more efficiently.

The staff reductions were connected to the DOGE initiative, which sought to cut federal spending. Social Security leadership is working to stabilize operations and prevent service disruptions for the millions of Americans dependent on retirement and disability benefits.

cards.headline: Major U.S. Automakers Pull Back From Electric Vehicles as Global Sales Boom
cards.teaser: The largest American car manufacturers have reduced their electric vehicle commitments even as worldwide EV sales continue to grow rapidly.
cards.body:
The largest U.S. automakers have reduced their investment in electric vehicle production at a time when global EV sales continue to accelerate. Manufacturers in Europe and Asia are expanding their electric vehicle portfolios and gaining market share during this shift.

The pullback by American automakers raises questions about their competitiveness as the industry transitions toward electrification and consumer preferences evolve. Industry analysts warn that this strategic retreat could disadvantage U.S. manufacturers in the long term.

cards.headline: Thames Water Returns to Profit After Raising Customer Bills
cards.teaser: The utility company reported a return to profitability but warned it only has enough debt funding to operate through the end of 2026.
cards.body:
Thames Water returned to profit after raising bills for customers, the company reported. The utility serves millions of households across London and the Thames Valley region, making it one of the largest water providers in the United Kingdom.

Despite the return to profitability, the company stated it only has sufficient debt funding to continue operations until the end of 2026. The financial pressure raises questions about the long-term viability of the company's current business model and whether additional rate increases or external financing will be required.

cards.headline: U.K. Proposes Midnight Social Media Curfew for Teenagers 16 and 17
cards.teaser: The government says the restriction would improve teenage wellbeing, but critics describe the proposal as a missed opportunity for more comprehensive reform.
cards.body:
The U.K. government is encouraging teenagers aged 16 and 17 to observe a midnight to 6am social media curfew, as part of Labour's effort to protect young people from online harms. Starting next spring, the curfew will be enabled by default on certain apps, though users can override it. The proposal also aims to disable "addictive" features such as auto-play and infinite scroll.

This measure extends the government's earlier announcement of a social media ban for under-16s. While officials say the curfew addresses sleep disruption and mental health concerns linked to nighttime screen time, critics argue the approach misses opportunities to tackle deeper issues like platform design and content moderation.

cards.headline: OpenAI plans first hardware device as movable speaker without screen
cards.teaser: The artificial intelligence company is developing a screenless smart speaker that can move and serve as an AI companion.
cards.body:
OpenAI is building its first consumer hardware product: a screenless speaker designed to function as an AI companion. The device will feature mechanical elements that can move on their own, setting it apart from stationary smart speakers currently on the market.

The product puts OpenAI in direct competition with established smart speaker manufacturers like Apple and Amazon. OpenAI has primarily focused on software development since its founding, making this venture into consumer hardware manufacturing a significant strategic shift.

cards.headline: NASA telescopes locate black hole in Omega Centauri star cluster
cards.teaser: Astronomers using NASA's Hubble telescope discovered a black hole inside a massive star cluster in the Milky Way galaxy.
cards.body:
Astronomers from the University of Utah used NASA's Hubble Space Telescope to detect a black hole in the Omega Centauri star cluster, located within the Milky Way galaxy. This marks the first confirmed discovery of what researchers believe could be thousands of similar objects hiding in the cluster.

Scientists have long theorized that Omega Centauri contains numerous black holes, but the dense concentration of stars made detection extremely challenging. This discovery provides the first concrete evidence of these "missing" black holes that researchers predicted existed in the ancient star cluster.

cards.headline: Samsung announces new foldable phones with Flex Titanium display technology
cards.teaser: The company confirmed it will reveal new foldable devices on July 22 featuring updated display materials designed to reduce creasing.
cards.body:
Samsung has unveiled Flex Titanium, a new flexible display technology designed to make foldable phones more durable and resistant to creasing. The company describes the technology as the result of lessons learned across seven generations of foldable devices. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Galaxy Z Flip 8 will be the first phones to feature this new display.

Samsung will reveal these new foldable models at an event on July 22.

cards.headline: SpaceX engineer's startup raises $65 million to modernize wire harnesses for aerospace
cards.teaser: A former SpaceX employee secured funding to develop updated wire harness systems for rockets, missiles, and satellites.
cards.body:
A startup founded by a SpaceX veteran raised $65 million to replace outdated wire harness technology used in aerospace applications. Wire harnesses bundle the electrical wiring that runs through rockets, missiles, and satellites, and current methods trace back to Cold War-era manufacturing processes.

The company aims to modernize how these critical components are designed and assembled. Wire harnesses represent essential infrastructure in aerospace systems, connecting electronic components and power sources throughout vehicles. The manufacturing process has remained largely unchanged for decades despite advances in other aerospace technologies.

cards.headline: PlayStation Store summer sale discounts games up to 75 percent
cards.teaser: Sony launched its seasonal sale with reduced prices on titles for PS5, PS4, and PSVR2 platforms.
cards.body:
Sony began its PlayStation Store summer sale on July 15, offering discounts of up to 75 percent on games across its console platforms. The sale includes titles for PlayStation 5, PlayStation 4, and PlayStation VR2 systems.

Among the discounted games are Ghost of Ytei Digital Deluxe Edition and Resident Evil: Requiem. The sale arrives as Sony faces criticism from some customers over its handling of physical disc support for games. More than 60 games are participating in the promotion, which runs through the summer season.

hero.headline: Spain advances to World Cup final after defeating France in semifinals
hero.body:
Spain secured their place in the 2026 FIFA World Cup final by defeating France 2-0 in their semifinal match in Dallas. Goals from Mikel Oyarzabal and Pedro Porro delivered a commanding victory that sends Spain to their first World Cup final since 2010.

Manager Luis de la Fuente highlighted the consistency of Spain's approach throughout the campaign. "We started almost four years ago with an idea and we've been faithful to that idea and it's brought us here," he said after the match. "Today we faced one of the best national teams in the world, but in front of them they had the best team in the world. These players deserve everything. Day after day they've shown their commitment, their solidarity, their generosity, their talent."

Spain's performance was described as a masterclass in control. The team demonstrated exceptional tactical discipline, with midfielder Rodri orchestrating play in his typical commanding style. Pedro Porro, named player of the match, credited the collective effort. "From the start to the end we played a great game," Porro said. "We knew we were facing a very tough team and we did everything so well. This is a team effort."

France manager Didier Deschamps acknowledged Spain's superiority while pinpointing his team's shortcomings. "Technically we were second best," he said. "The Spanish are very good at breaking up moves by reading interceptions and passes. We would have liked to cause them more problems going forward. I don't want to take anything away from Spain, a really good team which knows how to master its plan."

Spain's victory continues an impressive run of form. Since losing to Portugal on penalties in a Nations League final in 2023, Spain has won the 2023 Nations League and Euro 2024, reaching another Nations League final and now this World Cup final. The team has gone 38 competitive matches unbeaten.

Spain's squad showcased depth and skill throughout the performance. Players like Alejandro Balde, Gavi Olmo and Lamine Yamal demonstrated the attacking elegance that has defined Spain's tournament run. Young star Yamal, despite not scoring in the semifinal, played a significant role in Spain's victory and issued a statement of intent ahead of the final. "New York we're coming for you," he declared.

Spain will prepare to face the winner of the England versus Argentina semifinal on Sunday. The final will be held in New York. Spain's progression to the final represents a remarkable return to the sport's biggest stage, with De la Fuente's squad drawing comparisons to the 2010 championship team through their emphasis on tactical discipline and cohesive play.

cards.headline: American League shuts out National League 4-0 in All-Star Game
cards.teaser: The American League posted the first All-Star Game shutout since 2013 with a combined pitching performance.
cards.body:
Dylan Cease struck out the side in the first inning, then combined with 10 relievers to limit the National League to just three hits in the American League's 4-0 victory Tuesday night in Philadelphia. The dominant pitching performance marked the first All-Star Game shutout since 2013.

Cody Bellinger earned All-Star MVP honors after hitting a two-run single in the first inning. Ben Rice added an RBI single in the same inning as the AL built its winning margin early against Phillies pitcher Cristopher Sánchez.

cards.headline: Ben Stokes to play first match since England retirement
cards.teaser: The former England captain will return to action for Durham in the One-Day Cup next week.
cards.body:
Ben Stokes will make his return to competitive cricket next week, playing for Durham against Derbyshire in the One-Day Cup. The match marks his first appearance since stepping away from England duty.

The former England captain left international cricket and is now rejoining his county side for domestic competition.

cards.headline: Argentina manager Scaloni declines to mix football and politics before England semifinal
cards.teaser: Lionel Scaloni said he will not combine football and politics ahead of the World Cup semifinal.
cards.body:
Argentina manager Lionel Scaloni has stated he will not blend football and politics ahead of his team's World Cup semifinal clash with England. Scaloni made the comments as the two nations prepare for their high-stakes encounter.

England and Argentina are set to face off in the World Cup knockout stage, renewing their rivalry on football's biggest stage. The match carries extra significance given the historical tension between the two countries in previous World Cup meetings.

cards.headline: Wayne Rooney calls Jude Bellingham best player at World Cup
cards.teaser: The former England striker praised Bellingham's tournament performance and backed Harry Kane to deliver against Argentina.
cards.body:
Former England striker Wayne Rooney has named Jude Bellingham as the standout performer of the World Cup so far. Rooney praised the midfielder's displays throughout the tournament as England prepares for its semifinal clash.

Rooney also backed Harry Kane to make an impact in the upcoming match, expressing confidence in the striker's ability to be effective against Argentina.

cards.headline: 91-year-old Argentine journalist covering 18th World Cup
cards.teaser: Enrique Macaya Marquez has attended every World Cup since 1958, when a teenage Pele played.
cards.body:
Enrique Macaya Marquez, 91, is covering his 18th World Cup as an Argentine journalist. Since 1958, he has attended every tournament, beginning with the competition held in Sweden. His first World Cup featured a 17-year-old Pele.

Marquez's decades-long career reporting on the sport spans nearly seven decades of World Cup history, making his continued presence at the 2026 tournament a remarkable achievement in sports journalism.

cards.headline: Former teammates Will Keane and Harry Kane on different paths
cards.teaser: The two strikers who played together for England Under-19s face contrasting circumstances this week.
cards.body:
Will Keane and Harry Kane were once strike partners for England Under-19s, but this week they are on very different paths. Kane is preparing for England's World Cup semifinal, while Keane's career has taken a different direction.

Former England striker Wayne Rooney has praised Jude Bellingham as the best player at the World Cup so far, and believes Kane can destroy Argentina in the upcoming semifinal.

hero.headline: UK Government Proposes Social Media Curfew for Older Teens Alongside Under-16 Ban
hero.body:
The UK government has introduced a proposal to restrict social media access for teenagers aged 16 and 17 through a nighttime curfew, according to reporting by the BBC. Under the plan, platforms including Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube would be unavailable by default between midnight and 6 a.m. Teenagers in this age group would retain the ability to override the restriction manually. The measure accompanies a broader pending ban on social media use for children under 16.

The curfew proposal represents an expansion of existing government efforts to regulate youth access to digital platforms. While the under-16 ban aims to prevent children from accessing social media entirely, the curfew targets older adolescents with a more limited intervention. The default unavailability during overnight hours reflects concerns about sleep disruption and mental health impacts associated with late-night social media use among teenagers.

The government has not yet detailed how the curfew mechanism would be enforced or what technical measures platforms would need to implement. The override option for 16- and 17-year-olds distinguishes this approach from the outright ban for younger users, acknowledging a different level of autonomy for older teenagers. Implementation timelines and enforcement procedures remain unspecified in the current proposal.

The announcement places the UK among a growing number of jurisdictions exploring age-based restrictions on social media platforms. Australia recently implemented similar measures targeting youth access to digital services, and other European nations have considered comparable regulations. The approach reflects broader debates about balancing parental authority, individual freedom, and public health concerns related to social media use among young people.

The proposal will likely face scrutiny from technology companies, civil liberties advocates, and parents debating the effectiveness and appropriateness of government-mandated restrictions. Critics may question whether curfews can be effectively enforced given the technical sophistication of many teenagers and the global nature of digital platforms. Supporters argue that default restrictions provide a reasonable safeguard while preserving older teenagers' ability to make their own choices through the override function.

cards.headline: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle Meet With King Charles
cards.teaser: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle held a meeting with King Charles and Queen Camilla in the UK.
cards.body:
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle met with King Charles III and Queen Camilla during a rare visit to the United Kingdom. Queen Camilla adjusted her schedule to participate in the reunion between the King and his son. Prince William was not present at the meeting.

The gathering marks one of the infrequent occasions when the Duke and Duchess of Sussex have returned to the UK together since stepping back from royal duties. The meeting included the couple's children, though specific details about the encounter have not been publicly disclosed by the royal family.

cards.headline: Paddy Considine and America Ferrera to Lead Thriller Series 'Army of Shadows'
cards.teaser: Paddy Considine, America Ferrera, Alex Hassell, and Kit Harington will star in a new thriller series set in a near-future authoritarian Britain.
cards.body:
Ronan Bennett, the BAFTA-winning creator behind MobLand and The Day of the Jackal, has assembled a cast for his upcoming thriller series Army of Shadows. The ensemble will be led by BAFTA winner Paddy Considine, known for House of The Dragon and MobLand, alongside Oscar nominee and Golden Globe winner America Ferrera from Barbie and The Lost.

Alex Hassell and Kit Harington round out the principal cast for the series, which is set in a near-future authoritarian Britain. Bennett created and developed the project, which marks his return to television following his previous award-winning work in the thriller genre.

cards.headline: BBC Radio 1 Announces Schedule Changes With Multiple DJ Departures
cards.teaser: Three Radio 1 presenters will leave the station as part of a programming shake-up.
cards.body:
BBC Radio 1 will see the departure of Rickie, Melvin, and Dean McCullough as part of a broader schedule reorganization. The changes include adjustments to several shows across the station's programming lineup.

Jeremiah Asiamah will join Charlie Hedges on the Live Lounge as part of the restructuring. The departures and new appointments represent one of the more substantial programming adjustments for the network in recent months.

cards.headline: Timothée Chalamet Meets Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders at World Cup Match
cards.teaser: The actor attended a World Cup match at Dallas Stadium where he encountered the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders.
cards.body:
Actor Timothée Chalamet attended a World Cup match at Dallas Stadium on Tuesday night, where he was supporting France. During the event, he met members of the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders and appeared starstruck by the encounter.

The actor's attendance at the stadium drew attention from fans and media, particularly his interaction with the cheerleading squad.

cards.headline: Belgian Director Fabrice Du Welz to Lead Locarno Film Festival Jury
cards.teaser: Belgian filmmaker Fabrice du Welz will preside over the international competition jury at the 79th Locarno Film Festival.
cards.body:
Fabrice du Welz has been named president of the jury for the international competition at the 79th Locarno Film Festival. The Belgian director has made nine features that have screened at major festivals worldwide.

Locarno has previously shown two of du Welz's films, including Adoration. The festival announced jury members across multiple sections alongside du Welz's appointment to lead the international competition jury.

cards.headline: Locarno Competition Film 'The House on the Moon' Secures International Sales
cards.teaser: Singapore wuxia science-fiction feature secures worldwide sales representation ahead of its Locarno Film Festival premiere.
cards.body:
Parallax Films has taken on worldwide sales for The House on the Moon, a Singapore wuxia science-fiction feature from director Nelson Yeo. The film is set to premiere in the international competition at the 79th Locarno Film Festival.

The sales company holds exclusive rights across most international territories. German-speaking territories, Taiwan, and Singapore are excluded from that exclusivity, with Parallax holding non-exclusive rights in some other regions.

hero.headline: Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche faces confirmation hearing
hero.body:
Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche will appear before the Senate Judiciary Committee on Wednesday for his confirmation hearing to become the permanent leader of the Justice Department. Blanche currently serves as the department's number two official after winning Senate confirmation earlier in President Trump's second term.

The hearing represents a critical test as Blanche seeks to advance from his deputy role to attorney general. Lawmakers are expected to question him on his qualifications to lead the nation's chief law enforcement agency and his vision for the department's future. Democratic Senator Adam Schiff plans to participate in the questioning.

Blanche's confirmation process comes at a particularly contentious moment for the Justice Department. The agency has faced significant scrutiny over its handling of the so-called Epstein files. In February, Democrats accused the department of a "full-blown cover up" after Blanche declared the Epstein investigation effectively over, releasing what he said was approximately 3 million previously unseen documents. However, critics have raised concerns about the completeness and redactions in those releases.

More recently, investigative journalist Katie Phang filed a lawsuit in federal court on Monday alleging what she described as a "brazen, shocking, and ongoing violation" of the Epstein Files Transparency Act. The law, passed by Congress in November with a December 19, 2025 deadline for full document release, requires the Justice Department to publish all documents it holds about Jeffrey Epstein. Phang's lawsuit names Blanche as the defendant and accuses him of missing statutory deadlines, making improper or excessive redactions, failing to explain redactions as required by law, and withholding or retracting documents after release.

Blanche has argued that many redactions are necessary to prevent inadvertent identification of Epstein's victims, many of whom are minors. However, some Epstein victims have complained that their sensitive personal information was improperly exposed in the releases.

Democratic House Judiciary Committee ranking member Jamie Raskin stated in February that there were "tons of completely unnecessary redactions" in addition to failures to redact victims' names.

The Justice Department's Office of Inspector General announced last week that it is launching its own audit into the department's compliance with the Epstein Files Transparency Act. The preliminary objective of this internal inquiry is to evaluate the Justice Department's processes for identifying, redacting, and releasing records.

Phang's lawsuit seeks a court declaration that the Justice Department violated the law, orders for the release of all required documents without unlawful redactions, and the appointment of an independent special master from outside the department to oversee compliance.

If confirmed, Blanche would assume leadership of the Justice Department as it navigates these high-profile matters alongside numerous other federal law enforcement and national security responsibilities.

cards.headline: Forecast shows Democrats winning House, Senate split 50-50 in November
cards.teaser: A new projection from Decision Desk HQ puts Democrats on track to take the House while the Senate heads toward an even partisan divide.
cards.body:
Decision Desk HQ projects Democrats will win control of the House while the Senate remains evenly divided between the two parties heading into November's midterm elections. The forecast underscores how competitive the battle for Congress will be over 100 days before voters go to the polls.

A 50-50 Senate would leave the chamber deadlocked, with Vice President Kamala Harris holding the tie-breaking vote to determine which party controls the chamber. Democratic control of the House would allow the party to shape the legislative agenda and lead congressional committees.

cards.headline: Justice Department subpoenas New York Times journalists over Air Force One reporting
cards.teaser: The department issued subpoenas to four Times journalists over their reporting on security concerns about a Qatari-gifted jet for Air Force One.
cards.body:
The Justice Department has subpoenaed four New York Times journalists over their reporting on security concerns related to a jet offered by Qatar for Air Force One use. Federal agents delivered the subpoenas to reporters' homes over the weekend.

The action marks an escalation in Trump's long-running dispute with the Times. Critics argue the subpoenas represent an attack on press freedom, targeting journalists for exercising First Amendment protections to gather information in the public interest and protect their sources.

cards.headline: Government shutdown fears grow as Trump demands filibuster abolition
cards.teaser: Senators in both parties say shutdown odds are rising after President Trump called for eliminating the filibuster or facing a September spending battle.
cards.body:
The likelihood of a government shutdown in September is increasing after President Trump demanded that Republican leaders abolish the Senate filibuster or prepare for a spending confrontation. Trump issued the warning to GOP leaders, catching them off guard.

Senators from both parties acknowledge the rising risk of a shutdown. Trump's position sets up a potential showdown over government funding when current spending authority expires. The filibuster requires 60 votes to advance most legislation in the Senate, and abolishing it would allow the majority party to pass bills with a simple majority.

cards.headline: House Republicans work to advance third budget reconciliation bill
cards.teaser: GOP leaders aim to prepare a framework for another party-line budget bill by week's end despite internal divisions over priorities.
cards.body:
Republican leaders in the House are attempting to advance a third budget reconciliation bill by the end of the week. The effort aims to deliver a framework before the midterm campaign intensifies, though internal disagreements complicate the path forward.

President Trump has called for action on specific priorities through the legislation. Reconciliation bills can pass the Senate with a simple majority, bypassing the usual 60-vote threshold. House Republicans face competing pressures from different factions within their conference over what to include in the package.

cards.headline: Michigan Senate primary tests Democratic Party's direction
cards.teaser: The race between Representative Haley Stevens and Abdul El-Sayed is being viewed as an early indicator of the party's identity heading into 2028.
cards.body:
Democrats increasingly view the Michigan Senate primary as a significant test of the party's future direction beyond the midterms and into the 2028 presidential race. The contest pits Representative Haley Stevens against Abdul El-Sayed, who has backing from progressive figures including Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez.

The primary battle has already generated warnings within party circles about the stakes involved. Michigan's Senate seat represents one of several competitive races that could determine control of the chamber. The outcome may signal which wing of the Democratic Party gains momentum heading into the next presidential election cycle.

cards.headline: Trump administration renews military pressure on Iran over Strait of Hormuz
cards.teaser: President Trump is restarting confrontation with Iran in an effort to break its control over the strategic shipping channel.
cards.body:
President Trump is escalating military pressure against Iran in a bid to challenge its control over the Strait of Hormuz, a vital global oil shipping route. This represents a return to confrontational tactics from his earlier administration.

In response, Iran threatened to block all oil export routes in the region, citing the U.S. maritime blockade of Iranian ports. The renewed standoff echoes a pattern of military and economic pressure that has now persisted for more than four months, with experts questioning whether this approach will succeed where previous efforts did not.
